routes.name: Short stay without a visa
routes.summary: Many nationalities can visit for up to 90 days without a visa. Irish immigration says short breaks of under 90 days are allowed, but the page I could open did not list which nationalities are exempt. Check the official nationality list before you go. Schengen and UK visas are not valid for Ireland.

other: The visa-required vs visa-free nationality list is loaded by JavaScript on irishimmigration.ie and could not be read.
Everyone who is not an EEA national still faces immigration control on arrival.
A visa or visa exemption never guarantees entry. The immigration officer decides at the border.

routes.name: Short Stay C Visit/Tourist Visa
routes.summary: For visa-required nationals visiting for up to 90 days. Apply online through AVATS. A visa lets you travel but does not guarantee entry.

other: Only for nationals who need a visa for Ireland.

steps: Check if your nationality needs a visa on irishimmigration.ie.
Fill in the online application on AVATS.
Submit documents as the visa office instructs.
routes.processing: Check the Visa Decisions page for current processing times.

routes.name: Short Stay C Business Visa
routes.summary: For up to 90 days for meetings, negotiating or signing contracts. You can do work for 14 days or less if it starts and ends within one 14-day period. No work of 15 days or more, paid or unpaid.

other: Only for visa-required nationals.
Split work periods do not qualify. That needs the Atypical Working Scheme.

stay.note: Work limited to a single period of 14 days or less.

Irish Immigration: Visa fees

routes.name: Irish Transit Visa
routes.summary: Some nationals need a transit visa to pass through an Irish airport or seaport on the way to another country. Check irishimmigration.ie for your nationality.

other: Which nationalities need a transit visa, and airside transit rules, could not be confirmed from the pages I could read.

sources.label: DFA: Visas for Ireland
Irish Immigration: Visa fees

routes.name: UK Short Stay Visa Waiver and British Irish Visa Scheme
routes.summary: Some travelers coming from the UK can enter without a separate Irish visa under the Short Stay Visa Waiver Programme. Chinese nationals living in China and Indian nationals living in India may use the British Irish Visa Scheme (BIVS), one visa for the whole Common Travel Area.

other: Waiver requirements were not detailed on the pages I could read.
BIVS is for Chinese nationals resident in China and Indian nationals resident in India.

sources.label: DFA: Visas for Ireland

routes.name: Common Travel Area rights (Irish and British citizens)
routes.summary: Irish and British citizens have special rights to live, work and study in each other's countries under the Common Travel Area. Official pages I could open only mention this and do not explain the rights, so details need checking.

other: Detailed CTA rights text could not be read on official pages. Confirm on citizensinformation.ie or irishimmigration.ie.

sources.label: Citizens Information: Rights of residence in Ireland
DFA: Visas for Ireland

routes.name: EU/EEA/Swiss free movement
routes.summary: EEA nationals can travel to Ireland and do not need a residence permit to stay, with some limits. Non-EEA family members need a Residence Card of a family member of a Union citizen to stay over 3 months.

other: The detailed conditions (Article 7 of Directive 2004/38/EC) were not fully read.

sources.label: Citizens Information: Rights of residence in Ireland
Irish Immigration: Joining an EEA or Swiss national

routes.name: EU Treaty Rights family member (Residence Card)
routes.summary: Non-EEA family members of an EU/EEA/Swiss citizen using free movement. Without a residence card you need a single-journey C visa for up to 3 months. Staying longer means applying in Ireland for a Residence Card.

other: Qualifying family members include spouses, children under 21 and certain dependent relatives, and pay no visa fee.
Permitted family members pay the EUR 60 fee, refunded if approved.
You must show proof of the EU citizen's residence in Ireland at the port of entry.

sources.label: Irish Immigration: Joining an EEA or Swiss national
Citizens Information: Types of residence permission

routes.name: Critical Skills Employment Permit
routes.summary: For highly skilled workers with a job offer of at least 2 years. You can apply for a Stamp 4 when the permit is due to expire, and long-term residence after 60 months.

income.note: Strategic occupations on the Critical Skills list with a relevant degree. EUR 36,848 if the qualification is under 12 months old. EUR 68,911 for other eligible occupations.

other: Job offer must be for at least 2 years.
Nurses and midwives need a degree or diploma accepted by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Ireland.
No Labour Market Needs Test.
Employer generally needs 50% or more EEA staff, with a possible waiver for some start-ups.
Stay with the first employer at least 9 months, with exceptions.

stay.note: Offer must be at least 2 years. Stamp 4 for 2 years, renewable, is available at expiry.

routes.processing: Apply at least 12 weeks before the start date.

sources.label: DETE: Critical Skills Employment Permit

routes.name: General Employment Permit
routes.summary: The main work permit. Covers all jobs not on the Ineligible Occupations list. The employer applies and usually has to pass a Labour Market Needs Test first.

income.note: EUR 32,691 for some roles (horticulture, meat processing, health care assistant, home support). EUR 34,009 for recent Irish graduates.

other: Occupation must not be on the Ineligible List.
Labour Market Needs Test applies in most cases. Exceptions include salary of EUR 68,911 or more.
Employer generally needs 50% or more EEA staff, with some exceptions.
Stay with the first employer 9 months, with exceptions.
Spouse and dependants need their own permits.

stay.note: Renewals up to 3 more years. After 5 years with the same employer, renewal can be unlimited with no fee.

routes.processing: Apply at least 12 weeks before the start date.

sources.label: DETE: General Employment Permit

routes.name: Intra-Company Transfer Employment Permit
routes.summary: For senior managers, key staff and trainees moving from an overseas branch of a multinational to the Irish branch. It does not build long-term residence rights.

income.note: Senior management and key personnel. Trainees: EUR 36,605. The page also quotes EUR 46,000 and 34,000 in one place, so confirm the current figure.

other: At least 6 months with the overseas company before transfer (1 month for trainees).
The Irish branch applies.
Holder must go home when the permit ends.
Cannot be used to fill a vacancy permanently.

stay.note: Up to 5 years in total. Trainees up to 12 months.

routes.processing: Apply at least 12 weeks before the start date.

sources.label: DETE: Intra-Company Transfer Employment Permit

routes.name: Other employment permits (Contract for Services, Reactivation, Internship, Sport and Cultural, Exchange Agreement)
routes.summary: Five more permit types. Contract for Services is for staff of a foreign contractor on an Irish contract. Reactivation is for people who fell out of the system through no fault of their own. Internship is for non-EEA students abroad. Sport and Cultural is for sport and entertainment. Exchange Agreement is for reciprocal agreements.

other: Thresholds and fees were not checked. See each permit page on enterprise.gov.ie.

sources.label: DETE: Employment permit types

routes.name: Scientific Researcher on a Hosting Agreement
routes.summary: For researchers staying 3 months to 5 years at an accredited research institution. A visiting academic paid from outside Ireland can stay up to 12 months.

other: Details such as salary and exact permission were not checked.

sources.label: Irish Immigration: Coming to work for more than 90 days

routes.name: Start-up Entrepreneur Programme (STEP)
routes.summary: For non-EEA founders of innovative, high-potential startups. You get 2 years, renewable for 3 more. After 5 years you can apply for long-term residence. Retail, catering and personal services do not qualify.

other: Business must be an innovative high potential start-up under 5 years old, based and controlled in Ireland.
Aim to create 10 jobs and EUR 1 million in sales within 3 to 4 years.
You cannot take other employment and must not rely on state support.

Irish Immigration: Coming to work for more than 90 days

routes.name: Immigrant Investor Programme (closed)
routes.summary: Ireland's golden visa route. It closed to new applicants at the end of 15 February 2023. It required EUR 1 million, or EUR 500,000 for an endowment. Do not plan around it.

investment.note: EUR 500,000 for an endowment. From own resources, not a loan.

other: Closed to new applicants since 15 February 2023.
Approved investors got up to 5 years, renewable.

sources.label: Citizens Information: Coming to set up a business
Irish Immigration: Coming to work for more than 90 days

routes.name: Retirement / Independent Means (Stamp 0)
routes.summary: For people who can support themselves without working. You need about EUR 50,000 a year in income, private medical insurance, and no State benefits. You cannot work.

income.note: Individual income, pension or readily accessible money. Investments generally not counted.

other: Access to a lump sum for sudden major expenses.
Full private medical insurance covering private hospitals.
Police clearance and health declaration.
Visa-required nationals need a D-Reside visa first.
Register within 90 days of arrival.

sources.label: Irish Immigration: I want to retire to Ireland

routes.name: Student permission (Stamp 2 / 2A)
routes.summary: For full-time study on the Interim List of Eligible Programmes. Under 3 months use a C study visa, longer use a D study visa. Renew online when under 12 weeks remain.

savings.note: Access to EUR 10,000 for a one-year course, and for each later year, on top of fees. Shorter courses EUR 833 per month.

other: Letter of acceptance, proof of paid fees, English ability proof (unless an English course), private medical insurance.
Register with immigration for stays over 3 months.

steps: Get a letter of acceptance on an eligible course.
Apply for a C or D study visa online if you need one.
Register with immigration after arrival if staying over 3 months.

routes.name: Third Level Graduate Scheme (Stamp 1G)
routes.summary: Graduates with a level 8 or higher degree can extend their stay by 12 or 24 months to look for work.

other: Which degree level gets 12 vs 24 months was not confirmed.

sources.label: Citizens Information: Types of residence permission

routes.name: Working Holiday Authorisation
routes.summary: For young people from partner countries to travel and work casually for up to 1 year (2 years for Canadians). Places are limited. You must be outside Ireland to apply.

other: Taiwan has a separate scheme through Immigration Service Delivery.
Exact age limits were not stated on the page.
Enough funds for the early part of the stay and private medical insurance.
Register with immigration if staying over 90 days.
Short courses up to 6 months allowed.

sources.label: Irish Immigration: Working holidays in Ireland

routes.name: Join Family (non-EEA sponsor)
routes.summary: Spouses, civil and de facto partners, minor children and some dependent relatives can join a sponsor in Ireland. There is no automatic right. Income tests and waiting periods depend on the sponsor's category. Processing is reported as over 2 years.

income.note: Irish citizen sponsor: gross over the three years before applying, over and above state benefits. Other sponsor categories have different thresholds, for example over EUR 30,000 in the previous year for General Employment Permit holders (couple, no children).

other: De facto partners need at least 2 years of cohabitation.
General Employment Permit holders wait 12 months. Critical Skills holders, entrepreneurs and Irish citizens have no wait.
Sponsor must not have relied mainly on state support for 2 years.
Most students and Graduate Scheme holders cannot sponsor.

routes.name: Long-Term Residency
routes.summary: After 60 months of legal residence on employment permits you can apply for 5 years of permission to work without an employment permit. Self-employed applicants are not accepted.

other: 60 months on employment permits.
You must be employed when you apply.
No undue burden on the State, such as non-PRSI social welfare.
Good character. Absences generally under 90 days a year.

fees.label: Long-term residence fee, paid within 28 days of approval

routes.name: Naturalisation (5 years)
routes.summary: Needs 5 years of reckonable residence, with 1 continuous year right before applying. You must be of good character and plan to keep living in Ireland. The Minister decides. Most applications take about 12 months. Ireland allows dual citizenship.

other: 1 year continuous residence immediately before applying, plus 4 years in the 8 years before that.
Up to 70 days abroad in the year before applying.
No language test is listed on the pages read.
Attend a ceremony and make a declaration of fidelity.

citizenship.note: Ireland allows dual citizenship, but check whether your other country does.

routes.processing: Most applications processed within 12 months, per ISD.

routes.name: Naturalisation as spouse or civil partner of an Irish citizen
routes.summary: Married or in a civil partnership with an Irish citizen for at least 3 years. You need 3 of the last 5 years living on the island of Ireland, including 1 continuous year before applying.

other: Relationship must be genuine and enduring.
Live with your spouse or partner when you apply and when it is granted.
Good character and intent to keep living in Ireland.

sources.label: Irish Immigration: Naturalisation

routes.name: Citizenship by birth in Ireland
routes.summary: Born in Ireland before 1 January 2005: citizen. Born on or after that date: you are a citizen if a parent was an Irish or UK citizen, or had 3 of the 4 years of reckonable residence before your birth or an unrestricted right to live there. Born in Ireland with no right to another country's citizenship: citizen.

other: Student visa time and time awaiting an international protection decision do not count as reckonable residence.

sources.label: Citizens Information: Citizenship through birth or descent

routes.name: Citizenship by descent: Irish-born parent
routes.summary: If your parent was born in Ireland and was an Irish citizen, you are automatically a citizen even if you were born abroad. No application needed. You can apply for a passport.

other: Parent born on the island of Ireland.

sources.label: DFA: Registering a foreign birth
Citizens Information: Citizenship through birth or descent

routes.name: Foreign Births Register
routes.summary: Born abroad with an Irish-born grandparent, or a parent who was an Irish citizen at your birth? You can register and become a citizen from the registration date. Great-grandchildren qualify only if their parent was already registered when they were born. Cousins, aunts and uncles have no right.

other: Grandparent born on the island of Ireland, or a parent who was an Irish citizen at your birth.
Your children born before you registered are not eligible.
Apply online at fbr.dfa.ie. The form must be witnessed, then posted by recorded post.

citizenship.note: Citizenship starts from the registration date, not birth.

routes.processing: About 12 months for a complete application, in date order.
